Background (from the session that started this one):
AMU (PyPI `anti-messup`, command `amu`, repo github.com/abslock128w/AMU, remote named `github`) is a Python change-impact tool that posts a PR comment: it selects candidate tests from a static/lexical/co-change graph plus coverage, runs them on the base and head trees, reports flips, replays the PR's own tests on base, and shows side-by-side behaviour differences of changed functions on captured arguments. Current release v0.5.1 (main after PRs #71-#85). Numbers on a frozen 47-PR set from Django/sympy/Flask: first line correct 42/47, false behaviour rows 1, noisy comments 2, useful 19, false flips 0. See `evaluation/STATUS.md`, `evaluation/performance-v042/REPORT.md` (protocol, labels.json rubric, freeze.py/run.py), and `evaluation/ci/INSTALL-NOTE.md` (two-workflow GitHub Action: untrusted PR run + privileged comment post). A sympy fork pilot was done earlier the same way (fork, replay PRs, let the Action run). The owner has decided: no engine changes, no new features; the next evidence needed is AMU on a fifth codebase with a different shape, run live through the Action on the owner's own fork, never touching the upstream community repo. Owner rules: never run an upstream repo's test suite without asking once per repository (attrs is approved for this task); never commit keys; use `gh` (already authenticated as abslock128w); the owner is away, so do not stop for questions, record blockers and continue; standing authority covers merging your own PRs to abslock128w/AMU when CI is green and deleting your own branches. This checkout `/Users/Abslock128/Documents/ChatGPT/AMU/fix-base` is a git worktree of the AMU repo on branch `docs/status`; create your own branch from `github/main` for the report, do not switch this worktree's branch, do not commit to `docs/status`. Local recording/site-hook tests can fail on this Mac under load; GitHub CI is the arbiter.

Task:
Run an AMU pilot on a fork of `python-attrs/attrs`, entirely on the owner's GitHub. Never open an issue, PR or comment on python-attrs.

Steps:
1. Fork python-attrs/attrs to abslock128w/attrs with `gh repo fork`. Install the AMU Action on the fork exactly per `evaluation/ci/INSTALL-NOTE.md` (two workflows; comment posting on the fork only), pinned to AMU v0.5.1. Commit that to the fork's default branch.
2. Pick the last 15 merged upstream PRs that change Python under `src/attr/` or `src/attrs/` (skip docs-only, changelog-only, CI-only). For each, open a PR on the fork: base branch = a branch at the upstream merge-base commit (plus the AMU workflow commit), head = the PR's commits on top. Let the Action run live. Do not run anything locally that the Action should run.
3. For each PR record: job time from queue to comment, whether the comment posted, first line text and whether it is correct, useful/nothing/noise by the rubric in `evaluation/performance-v042/labels.json`, false behaviour rows, false flips, and what fraction of the attrs suite the budget covered (attrs' full suite is ~1 minute, so it should be all of it; report if not).
4. Measure two things not measured before: the per-PR cost of the Action on a small pure-Python project (job minutes), and whether side-by-side produces real rows on attrs' generated-class code.
5. If the Action fails to run at all on the fork, diagnose only enough to say why (secrets, permissions, runner, workflow), record it, and if it is an install-note error, fix the note in your report PR. No engine changes. Any engine defect gets a one-paragraph record with a reproduction, not a fix.
6. Write `evaluation/pilot/attrs/REPORT.md` with: the 15-row table, job-time range, budget coverage, the hand labels in `labels.json`, every defect, and a one-paragraph verdict on whether attrs is a fit for a maintainer ask. Open it as a PR to abslock128w/AMU on a branch from `github/main`, merge when CI is green.

Done looks like: 15 PRs on abslock128w/attrs each with an AMU comment (or a recorded reason for none), the report merged on main, and your final message starting with the 15-row table, then job-time range, then the verdict. Losses first.

# AMU on pull requests: install note and sample comment

For the owner's introductions to maintainers of Python repositories with slow suites.

## Install note (one paragraph)

AMU runs the tests that a pull request's diff reaches on both sides of the change, the merge base and the head, and
posts one comment listing the tests that flip from passing to failing. It edits that comment on every push, and it
never blocks a merge. To try it, copy two workflow files from
[github.com/abslock128w/AMU/tree/v0.5.0/ci](https://github.com/abslock128w/AMU/tree/v0.5.0/ci) into
`.github/workflows/` on your default branch. In `amu-pr.yml`, set both `install:` lines (the AMU job's and the optional
verify job's) to the command that installs your project and its test dependencies, test runner included: for sympy,
`python -m pip install -e . pytest hypothesis`.
- The first file runs your pull request's code under `pull_request`, with a read-only token, and only saves a JSON
  report. It must also be on any other branch pull requests target.
- The second posts the comment from `workflow_run` and never checks out or runs pull request code. GitHub runs it only
  from the default branch. Fork pull requests are covered without `pull_request_target`.
- By default AMU spends up to 300 s of test time per side, inside a 20-minute cap. On sympy the job took 9 to 12
  minutes. The comment follows when the posting job gets a runner, which took up to 15 minutes more while the
  repository's own CI held the runners.
- It caches its index keyed on the merge base. A cache saved by one pull request's job is visible only to that pull
  request's later pushes: a second pull request on the same merge base starts without it.
- With `counters: 'true'` it also keeps per-push counts and SHAs (never source or test names) in a hidden part of its
  own comment. Those let us measure whether its flips are real and whether they get fixed before merge. Nothing is
  sent anywhere else.

Remove the two files to uninstall.

## Sample comment

What a pull request that breaks one test sees (from a local run on a two-file repository):

> **AMU: 1 flip** at `9f3c2ab`, among 1 test run
>
> ### Flips (1)
>
> Pass on the merge base `41d07c2`, fail on the head. Each was rerun on the merge base to confirm it passed there.
>
> - `tests/test_calc.py::test_add`
>
> Rerun on the merge base in a fresh job: 1 passed again, 0 failed there too, so not the change, 0 could not be rerun.
>
> ### What ran
>
> 1 of 1 candidate tests on the head, 1.9 s with `pytest`, budget 300 s per side. Failures were rerun on the merge
> base. Tests outside the candidates were not run.
>
> <sub>AMU `0.2.0` from `v0.1.0`, report `1446af514737`. Full JSON is in the workflow run's artifact.</sub>

When nothing ran, the first line says so instead of giving a count. For example: "**AMU: no flip count** at
`9f3c2ab`: no candidate test ran". A runner that aborts on the head gets its own section, and anything AMU did not run
or could not see is listed under Gaps.

# AMU on pull requests, part 1 of 2: runs the pull request's code. Copy to .github/workflows/amu-pr.yml.
# Untrusted code runs only here, under pull_request, with a read-only token and no secrets. This job never
# comments; it saves its JSON as an artifact, and amu-pr-comment.yml posts it. Never use pull_request_target.
name: AMU pull request

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: amu-pr-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  amu:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      merge-base: ${{ steps.amu.outputs.merge-base }}
      flips: ${{ steps.amu.outputs.flips }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: abslock128w/AMU@v0.5.1
        id: amu
        with:
          # The command that installs your project and its test dependencies.
          install: python -m pip install -e .
          # counters: 'true'   # opt in: counts and SHAs kept in the comment, for the adoption measures
          # budget: '300'      # seconds of test time per side
          # wall-cap: '1200'   # seconds for AMU's whole run
          # observe: 'true'    # record the suite on the merge base when the cache has none
          # Generated probes for changed functions no test calls (C1): opt in by giving a key; the default caps are
          # $0.10 and 20 minutes per run. The key reaches this job, which runs the pull request's code: forks never
          # get it, but a same-repository pull request could read it.
          # anthropic-api-key: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
          # generate-dollars: '0.10'

    if: needs.amu.outputs.flips != '' && needs.amu.outputs.flips != '0'

    timeout-minutes: 20

        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.amu.outputs.merge-base }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: abslock128w/AMU@v0.5.1

# AMU on pull requests, part 2 of 2: posts the comment. Copy to .github/workflows/amu-pr-comment.yml.
# Runs from the default branch with a token that can comment. It never checks out or runs the pull request's code:
# it reads the saved JSON as data, takes the pull request and head from the trusted workflow_run event, and
# renders with AMU installed from a pinned tag.
name: AMU pull request comment

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [AMU pull request]
    types: [completed]

permissions: {}

jobs:
  comment:
    if: github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request' && github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'cancelled'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      actions: read
      pull-requests: write
      checks: write   # the informational AMU check with inline notes; it never fails
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          name: amu-report
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/amu-report
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          name: amu-report-verify
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/amu-verify
          run-id: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
          github-token: ${{ github.token }}
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
      - name: Post the comment
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          AMU_QUIET: 'true'   # one line when nothing was found; 'false' for every section
          AMU_REF: v0.5.1
        run: |
          python -m venv "$RUNNER_TEMP/amu"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/amu/bin/python" -m pip install --quiet --disable-pip-version-check --no-deps \
            "anti-messup @ git+https://github.com/abslock128w/AMU@${AMU_REF}"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/amu/bin/python" -P -m amu.ci.post --dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/amu-report" \
            --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --event "$GITHUB_EVENT_PATH" --verify-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/amu-verify"

name: AMU pull request check
description: Runs a pull request's candidate tests on its merge base and on its head, and saves which ones flip.

# This step always succeeds. What happened is in the saved JSON, not in the step's status.
# Linux and macOS runners only.

inputs:
  install:
    description: Shell command that installs the project and its test dependencies into the selected Python.
    required: false
    default: python -m pip install -e .
  python-version:
    description: Python for the project and for AMU (3.11 or later).
    required: false
    default: '3.12'
  runner:
    description: Test runner (pytest, unittest, django-runtests, django-manage). Empty means detected from the tree.
    required: false
    default: ''
  amu-ref:
    description: Tag of github.com/abslock128w/AMU that AMU is installed from.
    required: false
    default: v0.5.1
  base-sha:
    description: Base commit of the pull request.
    required: false
    default: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
  head-sha:
    description: Head commit of the pull request.
    required: false
    default: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
  artifact-name:
    description: Name of the artifact holding report.json and meta.json.
    required: false
    default: amu-report
  budget:
    description: Seconds of test time allowed per side (head, then merge base).
    required: false
    default: '300'
  wall-cap:
    description: Seconds for AMU's whole run, recording included. Past it the run stops and the comment says so.
    required: false
    default: '1200'
  observe:
    description: "'true' records the suite under coverage on the merge base when the cache has no recording."
    required: false
    default: 'false'
  cache:
    description: "'false' turns off caching of .amu/index (index and recording), keyed on the merge base."
    required: false
    default: 'true'
  counters:
    description: "'true' opts in to counters kept in a hidden block of the comment: counts and SHAs only, never source."
    required: false
    default: 'false'
  generate-dollars:
    description: "Dollar cap per run for model-written probes of changed functions no test calls (C1). Needs anthropic-api-key; '0' turns it off."
    required: false

  generate-minutes:
    description: Minute cap per run for generating and checking those probes.
    required: false
    default: '20'
  generate-model:
    description: Claude model that writes the probes.
    required: false
    default: claude-opus-5-5
  anthropic-api-key:
    description: "Anthropic API key for generated probes. Empty: none are generated. The job runs the pull request's code,
      so a same-repository pull request could read it; forks never receive secrets."
    required: false
    default: ''
  extras:
    description: "Comma-separated features still behind a flag, each off by default (renames and moves are labelled always):
      explore (a tenth of the candidate order for never-run tests), mutation (mutants on covered changed lines),
      equivalence (CrossHair and Hypothesis on annotated pure changed functions; both must be installed by install)."
    required: false
    default: ''
  claude-code:
    description: "'true' installs Claude Code on the runner and, when anthropic-api-key is empty, has `claude -p` write the
      probes, billed to the Claude plan as usage (generate-minutes still caps them). Off by default."
    required: false
    default: 'false'
  claude-code-oauth-token:

  - two of them share a merge base;
  - the recording (`observe`) was off.
- **Afterwards.** The pull requests were closed and their branches deleted. The fork is kept.

## Did every comment post

Yes: 10 of 10.

| Fork PR | sympy PR | AMU job | PR opened → comment | First line of the comment |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| #1 | 30690 | 490 s | 8.6 min | 0 flips among 1,760 tests run |
| #2 | 30693 (same merge base as 30690) | 539 s | 9.4 min | 0 flips among 2,600 tests run; 1 own test fails on the merge base and passes on the head |
| #3 | 30540 | 667 s | 17.7 min | 0 flips among 1,080; 10 own tests fail on the merge base, pass on the head |
| #4 | 30563 | 629 s | 11.0 min | 0 flips among 360; 1 own test |
| #5 | 30589 | 748 s | 26.5 min | 0 flips among 480; 18 own tests |
| #6 | 30590 | 602 s | 27.1 min | 2 flips among 760, both "fails as the test was before it was edited"; the verify job reran both on the merge base, both passed again |
| #7 | 30748 | 623 s | 25.2 min | 0 flips among 1,680; 1 own test |
| #8 | 30471 | 540 s | 26.0 min | 0 flips among 2,960 |
| #9 | 30701 | 621 s | 17.4 min | 0 flips among 1,760; 5 own tests |
| #10 | 30585 | 565 s | 11.4 min | 0 flips among 560; 2 own tests |

- **Job time:** median 612 s and worst 748 s, all under the 20-minute cap. Opened 8 at once, the jobs started within 4 minutes.
- **From open to comment:** 8.6 to 27.1 minutes. Opened 8 at once, the posting jobs queued behind sympy's own CI jobs on the account's runners (see below).
- **v0.3.0 fixes in delivery:**
  - On #30589, v0.2.6 executed nothing ("other side of the change could not be built"). Here it ran 480 tests and its 18 own tests gave change evidence: the patch-reverse fix (#32) at work.
  - On #30590, the two flips match the retrospective's.

## Cache on the shared merge base: miss

- #1 (30690) saved `amu-Linux-py3.12-319ea7a…`.
- #2 (30693) has the same merge base. Its log says "Cache not found for input keys: amu-Linux-py3.12-319ea7a…", and it saved the same key again.
- GitHub scopes a cache saved by a `pull_request` run to that pull request. Only caches saved on the base branch are shared, and the workflow never runs on the base branch. So the cache serves only a pull request's later pushes. The install note said "caches its index on the merge base", which reads as shared; it now says what happens.

## Where the note was wrong or unclear (fixed in this change)

1. **"set `install:`".** `amu-pr.yml` has two `install:` lines: the AMU job's and the optional verify job's. The note named one. Both need the project's install command, and for sympy that command must add the test runner (`pytest`, plus `hypothesis` for its tests): `pip install -e .` alone gives no runner.
2. **Where the files go.**
   - GitHub runs the posting workflow (`workflow_run`) only from the default branch.
   - The `pull_request` workflow runs from the pull request's merge commit, so it must be on the branch the pull request targets.

   The note said "copy … into `.github/workflows/`". It now says the default branch, and also any other target branch.
3. **The cache.** As above.
4. **Waiting time.** The note gave the time cap but not how long to wait. It now gives the job time seen here and the extra wait for a runner.

## What else happened, not the note's doing

- **sympy's own workflows ran too.** Its `test`, `Pyodide`, `Maintenance` and `zizmor` workflows run on every push to every branch, and on every pull request. Creating base and head branches started dozens of runs. I cancelled those started by the setup pushes. I tried to disable the workflows on the fork, and this session's permission check refused, so they also ran on the ten pull requests. That is the main reason the posting jobs waited.
- **`gh pr create` timed out several times** against GitHub's GraphQL API from this machine. The REST API worked.
- **Outside the fork:** nothing referenced the upstream pull requests. The bodies name them only as "upstream sympy pull request N", with no `#` and no link.

# AMU v0.4.2 on 47 fresh pull requests (2026-10-28)

Performance test, no engine change. Fresh pull requests only: frozen by `freeze.py` and committed (308c0b5) before any
run. Each was run as the v0.4.2 Action runs it (`run.py`), one at a time, and labelled by hand after reading its
description and diff.

## Results

| | Django | sympy | Flask | All |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Pull requests | 17 | 20 | 10 | 47 |
| First line correct | 12 of 17 | 17 of 20 | 8 of 10 | 37 of 47 |
| Adds something a reviewer would want | 6 | 7 | 2 | 15 |
| Adds nothing | 9 | 12 | 4 | 25 |
| Adds noise | 2 | 1 | 4 | 7 |
| Counted flips (unedited tests) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| … contradicted by the fresh-job rerun | — | — | — | 0 of 0 (never triggered) |
| Edited tests failing in their old form, set apart as "updated" | 8 | 32 | 2 | 42 |
| Behaviour-difference rows | 9 | 6 | 110 | 125 |
| … real | 0 | 6 (all intended) | 17 (all intended) | 23 (18%) |
| Median job time | 276 s | 295 s | 13 s | |
| Worst job time | 691 s | 452 s | 15 s | |

- **Flips:** none of the 47 pull requests broke an existing test it did not also edit. The 42 tests that passed AMU's
  flip checks were all tests the pull request edited, run in their old form. They are listed as "updated" and never
  counted, so the verify-flips rerun had nothing to check.
- **What adds something:** all 15 rest on change evidence. They are bug fixes whose new or edited tests AMU shows
  failing on the merge base and passing on the head, i.e. the tests reproduce the bug. Three add more:
  - Django #22137: a moved helper labelled as a move.
  - sympy #30803: behaviour rows showing that an EXRAW fix also changes the ordinary ZZ path.
  - Flask #5917: picks out the 2 of 11 edited tests that pin the fix.
- **Behaviour rows** were mostly wrong. Of 125, 23 were real (all intended by the author) and 102 were side-by-side
  artifacts (defects 1–3 below). Every behaviour row on Django and Flask that was not an intended API change was false.

## The comment was wrong or noisy on 13 of 47; the ten that matter most
  - Flask: the 10 most recent merged into `main` touching `src/flask/*.py`, any date.
  - Django had only 30 merges since the cutoff, 17 with production Python; the GitHub search total confirms 30. So
    Django has 17, not 20, and the test covers 47 pull requests, not 50.
- **Run (`run.py`):** `git archive v0.4.2` engine; merge base against head; budget 300 s per side; wall cap 1200 s;
  recording off; no generated tests; released defaults (rename labels on, other extras off); verify-flips when flips
  were counted (never); comment rendered quiet. Each repository's index cache was carried forward: Django and sympy
  from the Brief 5 cache, Flask cold. Job times are this machine's.
- **Environments:**
  - Django and sympy: the Brief 5 environments.
  - Flask: two venvs with its declared dependencies. PRs whose `uv.lock` pins pytest below 9.1 got pytest 9.0.2,
    because their conftest uses `_pytest.monkeypatch.notset`, which 9.2 removed. The rest got pytest 9.2.
  - A first Flask run on pytest 9.2 for all ten was discarded: 272 of 389 candidates unrunnable.
  - `tests/test_cli.py::test_get_version` fails on both sides because Flask is not installed as a package. It is
    never counted.
- **Labels:** `labels.json`, written after reading each description, diff and comment.
  - A first line is "correct" when its category (flips / behaviour difference / no test ran the changed code / adds new
    code only / refactor only / 0 flips on tested code) matches what the pull request is.
  - "No flip … whether any ran the changed code was not seen" counts as correct only where nothing better was knowable.
  - "Adds something" means something a reviewer cannot read from the diff and description.
  - Mechanical checks, such as an evidence test failing on the base, were rerun by hand where a label depended on them
    (Flask #5928).
- **Files:**
  - Comments: `<repo>/<n>.md`.
  - Report, meta and verify JSON per pull request: `reports.tar.xz`.
  - Upstream CI conclusions: `ci.json`.

# AMU v0.5.1 on 15 attrs pull requests, live through the Action (2026-11-02)

Fifth codebase, a different shape: attrs is small and pure Python, its suite runs in seconds, and most of its code
builds classes at run time. No engine change and no new feature. Everything ran on the owner's fork
[abslock128w/attrs](https://github.com/abslock128w/attrs). Nothing was opened, commented or pushed on python-attrs.

## Losses first

- **Two noisy comments, four wrong first lines (11 of 15 correct).**
  - Fork #1 (attrs 1636) says no test ran the changed `astuple` line. Eight attrs tests run it; AMU did not pick them
    (defect 1).
  - Fork #12 (attrs 1509) reports 62 behaviour differences, and all 62 are false (defect 3).
  - Fork #2 (attrs 1625) calls a fix to a typo in a comment "adds new code only" (defect 2).
  - Fork #5 (attrs 1571) says "whether any ran the changed code was not seen" where "adds new code only" was knowable
    (defect 4).
- **Side-by-side made no real row on attrs' generated-class code.** It compared 906 captured calls across 13 pull
  requests and found 0 differences, and none was expected. Its only rows were the 62 false ones.
- **Selection costs coverage here and saves nothing.** AMU ran 10 to 658 of attrs' ~1,400 tests: 0.7 % to 47 %, median
  35 %. The whole suite takes 3.9 s with plain pytest on a laptop. The 300 s budget was never the limit: the most any
  side used was 97 s.
- **Useful on 2 of 15.** Both are bug fixes whose new tests AMU shows failing on the merge base: attrs 1593 and 1513.
  attrs 1509 also had 13 such tests, but its 62 false rows make it noise.

## Results

| Fork PR | attrs PR | AMU job | Open → comment | Posted | First line (shortened) | Correct | Adds | False rows | False flips | Ran / suite |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| [#1](https://github.com/abslock128w/attrs/pull/1) | 1636 astuple nested atomics | 37 s | 62 s | yes | no test ran the changed code in `_funcs.py`; 10 tests run | **no** | **noise** | 0 | 0 | 10 / 1413 |
| [#2](https://github.com/abslock128w/attrs/pull/2) | 1625 comment typo | 34 s | 68 s | yes | adds new code only; no test of it ran | **no** | nothing | 0 | 0 | 468 / 1413 |
| [#3](https://github.com/abslock128w/attrs/pull/3) | 1606 evolve dunders | 64 s | 104 s | yes | no test ran the changed code in `_make.py`; 473 tests run | yes | nothing | 0 | 0 | 473 / 1413 |
| [#4](https://github.com/abslock128w/attrs/pull/4) | 1603 drop Python 3.9 | 132 s | 157 s | yes | 0 flips among 599, some on the changed code | yes | nothing | 0 | 0 | 599 / 1412 |
| [#5](https://github.com/abslock128w/attrs/pull/5) | 1571 `ne` validator | 55 s | 78 s | yes | no flip among 648; whether any ran the changed code was not seen | **no** | nothing | 0 | 0 | 648 / 1413 |
| [#6](https://github.com/abslock128w/attrs/pull/6) | 1592 generator on_setattr | 64 s | 98 s | yes | 0 flips among 658, some on the changed code | yes | nothing | 0 | 0 | 658 / 1408 |
| [#7](https://github.com/abslock128w/attrs/pull/7) | 1593 ClassVar forward refs | 55 s | 102 s | yes | 0 flips among 468; 1 own test fails on the merge base, passes on the head | yes | something | 0 | 0 | 468 / 1397 |
| [#8](https://github.com/abslock128w/attrs/pull/8) | 1600 defer imports | 59 s | 87 s | yes | 0 flips among 584, some on the changed code | yes | nothing | 0 | 0 | 584 / 1394 |
| [#9](https://github.com/abslock128w/attrs/pull/9) | 1541 converter decorator | 57 s | 84 s | yes | 0 flips among 473; 3 own tests fail on the merge base | yes | nothing | 0 | 0 | 473 / 1392 |
| [#10](https://github.com/abslock128w/attrs/pull/10) | 1529 fields() on instances | 68 s | 101 s | yes | 0 flips among 584; 2 own tests fail on the merge base | yes | nothing | 0 | 0 | 584 / 1387 |
| [#11](https://github.com/abslock128w/attrs/pull/11) | 1513 nested disabled() | 34 s | 70 s | yes | 0 flips among 101; 1 own test fails on the merge base | yes | something | 0 | 0 | 101 / 1384 |
| [#12](https://github.com/abslock128w/attrs/pull/12) | 1509 aliases before transformer | 92 s | 126 s | yes | 0 flips among 484; 13 own tests fail on the merge base; 62 behaviour differences | **no** | **noise** | **62** | 0 | 484 / 1383 |
| [#13](https://github.com/abslock128w/attrs/pull/13) | 1507 update dev | 71 s | 116 s | yes | 0 flips among 467, some on the changed code | yes | nothing | 0 | 0 | 467 / 1372 |
| [#14](https://github.com/abslock128w/attrs/pull/14) | 1454 ClassProps | 104 s | 134 s | yes | 0 flips among 595, some on the changed code | yes | nothing | 0 | 0 | 595 / 1372 |
| [#15](https://github.com/abslock128w/attrs/pull/15) | 1469 astuple common case | 43 s | 72 s | yes | 0 flips among 63, some on the changed code | yes | nothing | 0 | 0 | 63 / 1366 |

Totals:

| | attrs (15) | v0.4.2 set (47) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Comment posted | 15 of 15 | n/a (local) |
| First line correct | 11 | 42 (after v0.5.x) |
| Adds something a reviewer would want | 2 | 19 |
| Adds nothing | 11 | |
| Adds noise | 2 | 2 |
| Counted flips | 0 | 0 |
| False flips | 0 (verify job never triggered) | 0 |
| Behaviour rows: all / real | 62 / 0 | |

- **"Ran / suite":** tests AMU ran on the head, against tests pytest collects at that head. The collection was done
  locally on Python 3.14. That differs from the job's 3.12 only in which tests skip, not in how many are collected.
- **Full comments:** `comments/<attrs PR>.md`.
- **Per-pull-request numbers:** `data.json`.
- **Hand labels:** `labels.json`, same rubric as `evaluation/performance-v042/labels.json`.
- **Report, meta and patch per pull request:** `reports.tar.xz`. The workflow artifacts expire after 14 days.

## Job time and cost

- **AMU job:** 34 to 132 s, median 59 s. That includes checkout, `pip install`, indexing and both sides.
- **Posting job:** 13 to 19 s.
- **Wait for a runner:** 3 to 23 s. All 15 pull requests were opened within 40 s of each other.
- **Pull request opened → comment:** 62 to 157 s, median 98 s. On the sympy fork it was 8.6 to 27.1 minutes.
- **Cost per pull request:** 47 to 151 s of runner time, both jobs together.
  - Billed, with each job rounded up to a minute: 2 to 4 minutes, 38 minutes for all 15.
  - On a public repository those minutes are free. On a private one, at the standard Linux rate, that is about
    $0.016 per pull request at most.
- **Cache:** every job started cold, because the 15 merge bases were all different. The index took about 1 s to build
  (`seconds_before_running` 0.96 on #1), so the cache does not matter at this size.
- **Where AMU's time goes:** the test runs themselves.
  - AMU ran 599 tests in 96.9 s on attrs 1603. Plain pytest runs all 1,413 in 3.9 s.
  - So AMU's way of running a test list costs more than the whole suite would.
  - This is recorded only, not investigated: the job machine and the laptop differ, and the tests were run in
    AMU's fixed order.

## Budget coverage

- **The budget was never the limit.** The most test time used on one side was 96.9 s, out of 300 s.
- **AMU ran only its candidate tests:** 10 to 658 per pull request, 0.7 % to 47 % of the suite, median 35 %.
  - Tests outside the candidates were not run. Every comment says so.
  - On attrs this costs more than it saves. With the whole suite run, attrs 1636 would have run the 8 tests that
    reach the changed line, and its first line would have been right.

## Side-by-side on generated-class code

**Answer: it runs and agrees, but it produced no real row.**
- Side-by-side ran on 13 of 15 pull requests. It compared 906 captured calls of changed functions: attrs 1603 alone had
  533 calls of 5 functions, and 1600 had 111 calls of 8.
- On 12 of those pull requests it found 0 differences. That is right: none of them meant to change what a function
  returns.
- On attrs 1509 it reported 62 differences, all false:
  - The pull request adds a field to the slotted `Attribute` class.
  - AMU runs the changed methods on objects built by the old class, which has no slot for the new field (defect 3).
- attrs builds `__init__`, `__eq__`, `__repr__` and similar methods with `exec`. Those generated methods have no
  source lines in the diff, so side-by-side never targets them. Its targets are the builder functions in `_make.py`.

## Defects (recorded, not fixed)

1. **Candidate selection misses the tests that call the changed function through the package.** Seen on fork #1
   (attrs 1636).
   - **What happened:** `tests/test_funcs.py::TestAsTuple` calls `astuple` 20 times, imported as
     `from attr import astuple`. `src/attr/__init__.py` re-exports it with `from ._funcs import astuple`. AMU's 10
     candidates reach `astuple` only through `VersionInfo._ensure_tuple`, and none of them is in `TestAsTuple`.
   - **The first line is wrong:** it reads "no test ran the changed code".
   - **Reproduction:**
     1. Check out attrs at `ce52bb2`.
     2. Make line 304 of `src/attr/_funcs.py` raise.
     3. Run `pytest tests`: 8 `TestAsTuple` tests fail.
     4. The AMU report for fork #1 (`reports.tar.xz`, `1636/report.json`, key `tests`) lists none of them.
   - **Likely cause, not confirmed:** imports through a package `__init__` re-export in a `src/` layout are not
     resolved. The report says "1518 call sites unresolved repo-wide".
   - **Also seen on attrs 1469 (same function):** only the 4 `TestAsTuple` tests that pull request edits were
     candidates.
2. **A comment-only edit is called "adds new code only".** Seen on fork #2 (attrs 1625).
   - **What happened:** the diff fixes one comment line inside `Attribute.evolve`. The report has `adds_only: true` and
     `changed_functions: [Attribute.evolve]`.
   - **Why it shows:** `amu/ci/render.py` checks `adds_only` before `docs_only`, so the "docstring or comment changes
     only" line from #83 never shows.
   - **Reproduction:** `1625/report.json` in `reports.tar.xz`. Render it with `python -m amu.ci.render`.
3. **Side-by-side false rows on a slotted class that gains a slot.** Seen on fork #12 (attrs 1509).
   - **What happened:** the pull request adds `alias_is_default` to `Attribute.__slots__` and sets it in `__init__`,
     `from_counting_attr`, `evolve` and `_transform_attrs`. Run as changed on `Attribute` objects from the old class,
     those raise `AttributeError: 'Attribute' object has no attribute 'alias_is_default'`, or `TypeError`.
   - **The result:** 62 rows, all false.
   - **Why #78 did not help:** `input_built_before_the_change` is 0, so #78's set-aside for "failures on objects the
     old code built" did not fire.
   - **Reproduction:** `1509/report.json`, key `behaviour_differences`: 32 `TypeError` from `from_counting_attr`, 21
     `AttributeError` from `_transform_attrs`, 5 from `__init__`, 4 from `evolve`.
4. **Docstring edits next to a new function block "adds new code only".** Seen on fork #5 (attrs 1571).
   - **What happened:** the pull request adds `validators.ne` and edits docstrings in 12 existing validators. The first
     line falls through to "whether any ran the changed code was not seen".
   - **Why:** `adds_only` is false because existing functions changed, although each one changed only in its docstring.
   - **Reproduction:** `1571/report.json`.
5. **Unrunnable candidates are not named.** Seen on fork #5, #6, #10 and #14.
   - **What happened:** 15, 17, 41 and 15 candidates "could not be run by pytest". Neither the report nor the job log
     says which ones or why.
   - **On fork #10** a gap also reads "shadow run (after the change, pytest): no outcomes read: 1 error in 0.07s",
     with no further detail.
   - **Reproduction:** `1529/report.json`, keys `executed.unrunnable` and `gaps`.
6. **Code that only runs on another Python version is not called out.** Seen on fork #3 (attrs 1606) and #13
   (attrs 1507).
   - **What happened:** `add_replace` runs only on Python 3.13+, and the Action ran 3.12. On fork #3, "no test ran the
     changed code" is literally right, but the comment does not say the version is why.
   - **What it hid:** attrs 1507 is the pull request that started mutating `evolve`'s dunders, which 1606 later fixed. A
     3.12 job could not see it, and its comment says "some of them on the changed code" because other changed
     functions ran.

## Setup and install note

- **Install note:** followed as written, pinned to `v0.5.1`, both files on `main` and on each base branch. The Action
  ran on the first try on all 15, so there was no install-note error to fix.
- **Install line for attrs:** attrs keeps its test dependencies in `[dependency-groups]`, so the line is
  `python -m pip install -U pip && python -m pip install -e . --group tests`. `--group` needs pip 25.1 or later.
- **Suggested for the note, not changed here:** a sentence on `python-version:` for projects whose code branches on
  the Python version (defect 6), and the `--group` form of the install line.
- **The fork ran attrs' own workflows:**
  - Actions were already on for the fork, so the first push to `main` started attrs' CI, Zizmor and PyPI-package
    workflows. I cancelled them.
  - I then disabled attrs' 6 workflows on the fork, so only AMU's two ran. This is unlike the sympy fork, where the
    disable was refused. Runner waits here are therefore AMU's alone.
- **Replays:**
  - Each fork pull request's base is a branch `amu-base-<merge base>`: the upstream merge base plus one commit adding
    the two workflow files.
  - Its head is `amu-pr-<n>`, the upstream pull request's own head commit.
  - No two of the 15 shared a merge base.
  - Bodies name the upstream pull request as "upstream attrs pull request N", with no `#` and no link.
  - The pull requests are left open on the fork for reading.
- **Choice of pull requests:** the 15 most recent merged into attrs `main` that change a `.py` file under `src/attr/`
  or `src/attrs/`, from 1636 (2026-10-13) back to 1469 (2025-09-08).
  - Pull requests that changed none were skipped: dependabot, docs, CI, lockfile, and 1649 (`.pyi` only).
  - 1625 (a comment typo) and 1507 (`update dev`) change `src/attr/_make.py`, so they count.
- **Runs on this machine:** with the owner's approval for attrs, I collected the suite at each head to count it, and
  ran it twice at `ce52bb2`: once under coverage, and once with line 304 made to raise (defect 1). Nothing AMU does was
  run locally.

## Verdict

**attrs is not a fit for a maintainer ask.** AMU is pitched at slow suites. attrs' suite runs 1,400 tests in seconds,
and its CI already runs all of them on every Python it supports. That leaves AMU nothing to save and two ways to add
noise:
- **Selection:** it ran a third of the suite and missed the 8 tests that mattered on attrs 1636.
- **Side-by-side:** attrs' slotted, generated classes are where side-by-side is weakest. It produced 62 false rows on
  1509 and no real ones.

It added something on 2 of 15 pull requests, both by showing that a bug fix's new test fails on the merge base. On attrs
that is a few lines anyone can check in seconds.

**What this pilot does show:** the Action installs and posts correctly on a fresh fork with no help. A comment arrives
in under 3 minutes, at 2 to 4 billed minutes per pull request. It counted no false flips.

**For attrs-shaped projects, AMU would need two changes first:**
- run the whole suite on both sides when it fits the budget;
- set aside side-by-side failures caused by a slot or field the old class lacks.

Both are engine changes, outside this pilot.

The pilot is done: all 15 replay PRs on abslock128w/attrs have an AMU comment, and the report is open as [abslock128w/AMU#86](https://github.com/abslock128w/AMU/pull/86). It is **not merged yet**: CI on #86 was still pending, and I'll merge it when the app reports the checks green.

| Fork PR | attrs PR | AMU job | Open → comment | Posted | First line | Correct | Adds | False rows | False flips | Ran / suite |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| #1 | 1636 astuple tweak | 37 s | 62 s | yes | no test ran the changed code; 10 run | **no** | **noise** | 0 | 0 | 10 / 1413 |

| #12 | 1509 aliases | 92 s | 126 s | yes | 0 flips; 13 own tests; 62 behaviour differences | **no** | **noise** | **62** | 0 | 484 / 1383 |
| #13 | 1507 update dev | 71 s | 116 s | yes | 0 flips | yes | nothing | 0 | 0 | 467 / 1372 |
| #14 | 1454 ClassProps | 104 s | 134 s | yes | 0 flips | yes | nothing | 0 | 0 | 595 / 1372 |
| #15 | 1469 astuple | 43 s | 72 s | yes | 0 flips | yes | nothing | 0 | 0 | 63 / 1366 |

**Losses:**
- **Wrong first lines:** 4 of 15 (11 correct).
- **Noise:** 2 comments.
  - On #12 (attrs 1509), all 62 behaviour rows are false. The PR adds a slot to a class, and AMU ran the new methods on objects of the old class, which has no such slot.
  - On #1 (attrs 1636), the comment says no test ran the changed line. Eight attrs tests do run it, and AMU didn't pick any. I confirmed this by making the line raise: those 8 fail.
- **Useful:** only 2 of 15.
- **False flips:** none.

**Job time:**
- **AMU job:** 34–132 s, median 59 s.
- **Posting job:** 13–19 s.
- **PR opened to comment:** 62–157 s, against 9–27 minutes on the sympy fork.
- **Cost:** 2–4 billed minutes per PR, 38 minutes for all 15, free on a public repo.

**Budget coverage:** AMU never ran the whole suite. It ran 0.7–47 % of attrs' ~1,400 tests (median 34 %), choosing them itself; the 300 s budget was never the limit (the most used was 97 s). The full suite takes 3.9 s.

**Side-by-side on generated-class code:** it compared 818 calls across 12 PRs with 0 differences, as expected. Its only rows were the 62 false ones, so it produced no real rows on attrs.

**Verdict:** attrs is not a fit for a maintainer ask. Its suite runs in seconds and its CI already runs all of it, so AMU has nothing to save. Its two noise sources hit attrs directly: test selection missed the tests that mattered, and side-by-side mishandles attrs' slotted, generated classes. What this pilot does show is that the Action installs and posts correctly on a fresh fork, with no help and no install-note errors.

**Engine defects (recorded with reproductions, not fixed):**
1. Tests that import the changed function from the package (`from attr import astuple`) are not picked.
2. A comment-only edit gets the first line "adds new code only".
3. Side-by-side gives false rows when a slotted class gains a slot.
4. Docstring edits next to a new function stop "adds new code only" from showing.
5. Tests AMU couldn't run (15–41 per PR, on 4 PRs) are not named anywhere.
6. Code that only runs on Python 3.13+ is not called out. Because of this, AMU never ran the change in attrs 1507 that 1606 later fixed.

**Things I did on the fork:**
- I disabled attrs' own six workflows there, after its first push started attrs' CI. Timings are AMU's alone.
- The attrs install line needs `--group tests` plus a pip upgrade. The report suggests adding that and a `python-version:` note to the install note; I didn't change the note.
- I left the 15 PRs open on the fork for reading.

The report, labels, per-PR data and archived AMU reports are in `evaluation/pilot/attrs/` on branch `eval/attrs-pilot`.

44	def changed_symbols(root, facts, edits, gaps):
45	    """Map changed lines to symbols.
46	
47	    Returns {identity: fallback}: the narrowest declaration holding each changed
48	    line, with the enclosing class as a fallback for unresolved receivers.
49	    Enclosing functions hold the line too and are changed in their own right.
50	    """
51	    changed, where = {}, {}
52	    for path, edit in edits.items():
53	        records = facts.get(path, {}).get('records', {})
54	        if not records:
55	            gaps.append(f'{path}: not in the tree; new code has no existing callers')
56	            continue
57	        # An agent may ask before or after writing its edit; use whichever side the tree holds.
58	        if applied(root, path, edit):
59	            # Removed lines left no line of their own; they count where their replacement or neighbour now sits.
60	            place = renumber(edit)
61	            lines = edit['new'] | {place(line) for line in edit['old']}
62	        else:
63	            lines = edit['old'] | edit['anchor']
64	        for line in sorted(lines):
65	            containing = sorted((r for r in records.values() if any(a <= line <= b for a, b in r['spans'])),
66	                                key=lambda r: (r['kind'] == 'module', min(b - a for a, b in r['spans'])))
67	            if not containing:

70	            classes = [r['id'] for r in containing[1:] if r['kind'] == 'class']
71	            changed.setdefault(narrow['id'], classes[0] if classes and narrow['kind'] != 'class' else None)

73	            for outer in containing[1:]:

                PYTHONPATH=str(ENGINE))


def environment_name(name, head):
    """The interpreter the project's own install would give: Flask pins pytest in uv.lock, and its conftest used
    pytest's private ``monkeypatch.notset`` until pytest 9.1 removed it; such a pull request gets env/flask-p90
    (pytest 9.0.2), the rest env/flask (pytest 9.2). Django and sympy use their retrospective environments."""
    if name != 'flask':
        return name
    lock = (head/'uv.lock').read_text() if (head/'uv.lock').exists() else ''
    pin = next((line.split('"')[1] for prev, line in zip(lock.splitlines(), lock.splitlines()[1:])
                if prev == 'name = "pytest"'), '')
    major_minor = tuple(int(p) for p in pin.split('.')[:2]) if pin else (99, 0)

    python = str(ROOT/'env'/environment_name(name, head)/'bin'/'python')

"""Side-by-side execution of changed functions on captured inputs (Python 3.12 and later).

While candidate tests run on the code before the change, a sys.monitoring hook watches the changed functions. When one
starts, its arguments are snapshotted with pickle (a deep copy that also bounds size), and the function is executed
right there, in the test's own process and state, twice in its version before the change and twice in its version
after, each time on a fresh copy of the arguments. Compared: the return value (or the exception raised), the arguments
afterwards (mutation), what was printed, and the sequence of calls made from first-party code to code outside it. A
difference is kept only when both versions repeat themselves exactly; one that does not is nondeterministic and dropped.

Both versions are compiled from source the same way (decorators left off, so a wrapper's own behaviour is not compared),
in the module's globals, with ``__class__`` bound for ``super()`` and their own name looked up in those globals, as in the
module (recursion reaches the version swapped in for the run); a decorated module function's own name is the copy itself,
so its recursion is undecorated too. Each is named as the source names it, as is everything defined in it. Then the
test's own call goes on as usual. A function that is nested, a coroutine, a generator on one side only, or a method using
a private name that a class body would mangle is not compared, and is counted as such; so is a function in a test file
(the tests, not the code they test), and one whose code is the same once its docstring is set aside (only the docstring,
comments or layout changed).

This runs the project's code on inputs it was really called with; it is a run of its own on the code before the change,
separate from the comparison of test outcomes, whose results it does not touch.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import ast
import copy
import json
import re
import textwrap
from pathlib import Path

from . import replay, runners

KIND = 'behaviour differs on captured input'
CALLS = 5          # calls captured per argument shape of a changed function, per process
SHAPES = 8         # argument shapes sampled per changed function, per process
LISTED = 100       # captured calls named in the report
PRIVATE = re.compile(r'(?<![\w.])__[A-Za-z]\w*(?<!__)\b')

HOOK = r'''
import os as _os, sys as _sys
_spec_path = _os.environ.get("AMU_SBS_SPEC")
if _spec_path and _sys.version_info >= (3, 12):
    try:
        import contextlib, copy, inspect, io, json, pickle, re, textwrap, threading, types
        with open(_spec_path) as _h:
            _spec = json.load(_h)
        _out = _os.environ["AMU_SBS_OUT"]
        _root = _os.path.realpath(_spec["root"]) + _os.sep
        _m = _sys.monitoring
        _tool = next(i for i in (3, 4, 5) if _m.get_tool(i) is None)
        _m.use_tool_id(_tool, "amu-side-by-side")
        _want = {(_os.path.realpath(t["file"]), t["qual"]): t for t in _spec["targets"]}
        _files = {k[0] for k in _want}
        _keys, _built, _count = {}, {}, {}
        _local = threading.local()
        _journal = _os.path.join(_out, "%d.jsonl" % _os.getpid())

        def _emit(kind, **data):
            """One line per event, written at once: a run stopped at its time limit keeps what it compared."""
            try:
                with open(_journal, "a") as handle:
                    handle.write(json.dumps(dict(data, kind=kind)) + "\n")
            except Exception:
                pass
        _limit = _spec.get("calls", 5)
        _shapes = _spec.get("shapes", 8)
        _taken = {}
        _bytes = _spec.get("bytes", 262144)
        _ADDRESS = re.compile(r" at 0x[0-9a-fA-F]+")
        _GEN = 0x20 | 0x80 | 0x100 | 0x200

        def _key(code):
            found = _keys.get(code)
            if found is None:
                name = code.co_filename
                path = _os.path.realpath(name) if name and not name.startswith("<") else ""
                found = _keys[code] = (path, code.co_qualname) if path in _files else False
            return found

        def _fp(value, depth=0, seen=None):
            """A comparable fingerprint: structure for builtin containers and plain objects, never getattr on them."""
            seen = seen if seen is not None else set()
            kind = type(value)
            if value is None or kind in (bool, int, float, complex, str, bytes):
                return repr(value)
            if depth > 4 or id(value) in seen:
                return "<" + kind.__qualname__ + ">"
            seen = seen | {id(value)}
            if kind in (list, tuple, set, frozenset):
                items = [_fp(v, depth + 1, seen) for v in value]
                return [kind.__name__, sorted(items, key=repr) if kind in (set, frozenset) else items]
            if kind is dict:
                return ["dict", sorted(([_fp(k, depth + 1, seen), _fp(v, depth + 1, seen)] for k, v in value.items()), key=repr)]
            try:
                state = object.__getattribute__(value, "__dict__")
            except Exception:
                state = None
            if type(state) is dict and kind.__repr__ is object.__repr__:
                return [kind.__module__ + "." + kind.__qualname__, _fp(state, depth + 1, seen)]
            try:
                text = repr(value)
            except Exception as exc:
                text = "<repr failed: " + type(exc).__name__ + ">"
            return kind.__qualname__ + ":" + _ADDRESS.sub(" at 0x?", text)[:2000]

        def _requalified(code, wrapper, owner):
            """``code`` with each qualified name in it (functions, generators, coroutines, classes) that starts with
            ``wrapper`` starting with ``owner`` instead: what is built inside a wrapper is named as in the source
            (sympy #30715: a generator's outcomes differed only in "__amu_outer__.<locals>.")."""
            consts = tuple(_requalified(c, wrapper, owner) if type(c) is types.CodeType
                           else owner + c[len(wrapper):] if type(c) is str and c.startswith(wrapper) else c
                           for c in code.co_consts)  # a class body stores its __qualname__ as a constant
            name = code.co_qualname
            name = owner + name[len(wrapper):] if name.startswith(wrapper) else name
            return code.replace(co_consts=consts, co_qualname=name)

        def _build(target, which, globs):
            source = target.get(which)
            if source is None:
                return None
            parts = target["qual"].split(".")
            # Its own name is a global, as in its module (a function recursing, a method calling the module function it
            # is named after), not a cell of the wrapper holding the owner. A module function whose name holds something
            # else (a decorator's wrapper, a cache) reaches the copy itself, so its recursion is undecorated on both sides:
            # the as-changed run swaps such a wrapper for the bare copy.
            own = globs.get(target["name"])
            itself = len(parts) == 1 and not (type(own) is types.FunctionType and _want.get(_key(own.__code__)) is target)
            if which == "after":
                _prepare_swaps()
                _swapped(True)
            template = ("def __amu_outer__():\n" + ("" if itself else "    global " + target["name"] + "\n")
                        + "    __class__ = None\n" + textwrap.indent(source, "    ") + "\n    return " + target["name"] + "\n")
            space = dict(globs)
            try:
                code = _requalified(compile(template, target["file"], "exec"), "__amu_outer__.<locals>.",
                                    target["qual"][:-len(target["name"])])
                if not itself:
                    # The global declaration names the copy, and what it defines, as a module function's.

"""The execution recorder: watched lines per test and calls into watched functions, from a side's own run."""
import subprocess
import sys
import textwrap

import pytest

from amu.core import record, runners

pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(sys.version_info < (3, 12), reason='sys.monitoring needs Python 3.12')

PACKAGE = {
    'src/pkg/__init__.py': 'from ._impl import shape, Box\n',
    'src/pkg/__init__.pyi': 'def shape(value: object) -> str: ...\nclass Box: ...\n',
    'src/pkg/_impl.py': textwrap.dedent('''\
        def shape(value):
            if isinstance(value, list):
                return "list"
            return "other"


        class Box:
            __slots__ = ("size",)

            def __init__(self, size):
                self.size = size

            def grow(self, by):
                self.size += by
                return self.size
        '''),
    'tests/test_shape.py': textwrap.dedent('''\
        from pkg import shape, Box


        def test_list():
            assert shape([1]) == "list"


        def test_other():
            assert shape(3) == "other"


        def test_box():
            assert Box(2).grow(1) == 3


        def test_nothing():
            assert True
        '''),
    'tests/test_unit.py': textwrap.dedent('''\
        import unittest

        from pkg import shape


        class ShapeCase(unittest.TestCase):
            def test_list(self):
                self.assertEqual(shape([]), "list")
        '''),
}


def project(tmp_path):
    for name, text in PACKAGE.items():
        (tmp_path/name).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (tmp_path/name).write_text(text)
    return tmp_path


def run(tmp_path, command, lines, targets, cwd=None):
    env = runners.environment(tmp_path, record.prepare(tmp_path/'.rec', tmp_path, lines, targets))
    done = subprocess.run(command, cwd=cwd or tmp_path, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=120)
    assert done.returncode in (0, 1), done.stdout + done.stderr
    return record.read(tmp_path/'.rec', tmp_path, cwd)


def test_each_test_is_credited_with_the_watched_lines_it_ran_however_it_imported_them(tmp_path):
    # The tests reach shape through the package's re-export, with a stub beside it: no name resolution is involved.
    project(tmp_path)
    coverage, calls, _ = run(tmp_path, [sys.executable, '-m', 'pytest', '-q', '-p', 'no:cacheprovider', 'tests/test_shape.py'],
                             {'src/pkg/_impl.py': [3, 4]}, [])
    assert record.tests_on(coverage, 'src/pkg/_impl.py', [3]) == {'tests/test_shape.py::test_list'}, coverage
    assert record.tests_on(coverage, 'src/pkg/_impl.py', [4]) == {'tests/test_shape.py::test_other'}, coverage
    assert 'tests/test_shape.py::test_nothing' not in coverage
    assert calls == []


def test_unittest_ids_resolve_to_their_file(tmp_path):
    project(tmp_path)
    coverage, _, _ = run(tmp_path, [sys.executable, '-m', 'unittest', '-v', 'tests.test_unit'], {'src/pkg/_impl.py': [3]}, [])
    assert record.tests_on(coverage, 'src/pkg/_impl.py', [3]) == {'tests/test_unit.py::ShapeCase::test_list'}, coverage


def test_calls_carry_digests_of_input_and_output_and_slotted_state_is_part_of_the_input(tmp_path):
    project(tmp_path)
    targets = [('src/pkg/_impl.py', 'shape'), ('src/pkg/_impl.py', 'Box.grow')]
    _, calls, _ = run(tmp_path, [sys.executable, '-m', 'pytest', '-q', '-p', 'no:cacheprovider', 'tests/test_shape.py'], {}, targets)
    by = {(c['test'], c['function']): c for c in calls}
    grow = by['tests/test_shape.py::test_box', 'src/pkg/_impl.py#Box.grow']
    assert '"size"' in grow['input_shown'] and '"2"' in grow['input_shown'], grow  # the slot's value is in the input
    assert grow['output_shown'] == '["return", "3"]', grow
    assert by['tests/test_shape.py::test_list', 'src/pkg/_impl.py#shape']['output_shown'] == '["return", "\'list\'"]'
    # The same call made again gives the same digests: they are stable across processes.

"""A change as hunks, and the lines that tell whether a test ran each one.

Each hunk of a changed Python file gets two sets of lines to watch while the tests run:

- on the code before the change (``base``): the body of the innermost function holding the hunk there, so any test that
  entered that function counts; for a hunk outside any function, its removed lines and the context lines around it;
- on the code after it (``head``): the lines the hunk adds, or, for a hunk that only removes, the lines around the gap.

A hunk with no function around it on the base side and nothing it removed there (code the change adds, such as a new
function) has no base lines: no run of the code before the change can say which tests reach it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import ast


def _functions(text):
    """[(first body line, last line, qualified name)] of every function in ``text``; [] when it does not parse."""
    try:
        tree = ast.parse(text or '')
    except (SyntaxError, ValueError):
        return []
    found = []

    def walk(nodes, prefix):
        for node in nodes:
            if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
                qual = prefix + node.name
                if node.body:
                    found.append((node.body[0].lineno, node.end_lineno, qual))
                walk(node.body, qual + '.<locals>.')
            elif isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef):
                walk(node.body, prefix + node.name + '.')
            elif hasattr(node, 'body') and isinstance(getattr(node, 'body'), list):
                walk(node.body, prefix)
                walk(getattr(node, 'orelse', []) or [], prefix)
                walk(getattr(node, 'finalbody', []) or [], prefix)
                for handler in getattr(node, 'handlers', []) or []:
                    walk(handler.body, prefix)
    walk(tree.body, '')
    return found


def innermost(functions, lines):
    """The narrowest function whose body holds every line in ``lines``, as (first, last, qual); None if none does."""
    lines = sorted(lines)
    if not lines:
        return None
    holding = [f for f in functions if f[0] <= lines[0] and lines[-1] <= f[1]]
    return min(holding, key=lambda f: f[1] - f[0]) if holding else None


def split(path, edit, before, after):
    """The hunks of one file's change, each a dict: path, index, removed and added line numbers, context lines on each
    side, the function holding it on each side, and the lines to watch on each side (``base``, ``head``)."""
    old_functions, new_functions = _functions(before), _functions(after)
    found = []
    for index, (old_start, body, new_start) in enumerate(edit.get('hunks', [])):
        old_line, new_line = old_start, new_start
        removed, added, old_context, new_context = [], [], [], []
        for row in body:
            sign = row[:1]
            if sign == '-':
                removed.append(old_line)
                old_line += 1
            elif sign == '+':
                added.append(new_line)
                new_line += 1
            else:
                old_context.append(old_line)
                new_context.append(new_line)
                old_line += 1
                new_line += 1
        # Where the hunk sits on each side: what it removes or adds, else the gap between its context lines.
        old_here = removed or [n for n in old_context if n < (old_context[-1] if old_context else 0)][-1:] or old_context[:1]
        new_here = added or [n for n in new_context if n < (new_context[-1] if new_context else 0)][-1:] or new_context[:1]
        old_function = innermost(old_functions, removed or old_here)
        new_function = innermost(new_functions, added or new_here)
        if old_function:
            base = set(range(old_function[0], old_function[1] + 1))
        elif removed:
            base = set(removed) | set(old_context)
        elif new_function is None:
            base = set(old_context)  # module or class level: the lines around the insertion run when it runs
        else:
            base = set()  # inside a function the code before the change does not have
        head = set(added) if added else set(new_context)
        found.append(dict(path=path, index=index, removed=removed, added=added, old_start=old_start, new_start=new_start,
                          old_function=old_function[2] if old_function else None,
                          new_function=new_function[2] if new_function else None,
                          base=sorted(base), head=sorted(head)))
    return found


def name(hunk):
    """``path:line`` where the hunk starts on the code after the change."""
    line = (hunk['added'] or [hunk['new_start']])[0]
    return f"{hunk['path']}:{line}"

"""Execution-first selection: the candidates come from what the tests were seen to run, not from name resolution."""
import difflib
import json
import sys
import textwrap

import pytest

from amu.core import analyze

pytestmark = pytest.mark.skipif(sys.version_info < (3, 12), reason='sys.monitoring needs Python 3.12')

IMPL = textwrap.dedent('''\
    def shape(value):
        if isinstance(value, list):
            return [shape(v) for v in value]
        return type(value).__name__
    ''')
FILES = {
    # A package that re-exports, beside a stub of the same module: resolving `from pkg import shape` by name finds the
    # stub's declaration, not the code.
    'src/pkg/__init__.py': 'from ._impl import shape as shape\n',
    'src/pkg/__init__.pyi': 'def shape(value: object) -> object: ...\n',
    'src/pkg/_impl.py': IMPL,
    'tests/test_shape.py': textwrap.dedent('''\
        import pkg


        def test_nested():
            assert pkg.shape([1, [2]]) == ["int", ["int"]]


        def test_flat():
            assert pkg.shape(1) == "int"
        '''),
    'tests/test_other.py': 'def test_unrelated():\n    assert 1 + 1 == 2\n',
}


def change(tmp_path, after_impl, **kwargs):
    for name, text in FILES.items():
        (tmp_path/name).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (tmp_path/name).write_text(text)
    (tmp_path/'src/pkg/_impl.py').write_text(after_impl)
    diff = ''.join(difflib.unified_diff(IMPL.splitlines(True), after_impl.splitlines(True), 'a/src/pkg/_impl.py', 'b/src/pkg/_impl.py'))
    return analyze(tmp_path, diff, full_evidence=True, index_dir=tmp_path/'.index', run=True, python=sys.executable, **kwargs)


BROKEN = IMPL.replace('return [shape(v) for v in value]', 'return [shape(v) for v in value][::-1]')


def test_a_suite_that_fits_runs_whole_on_both_sides(tmp_path):
    report = change(tmp_path, BROKEN)
    assert report['selection_evidence']['mode'] == 'all of the suite', report['selection_evidence']
    assert report['executed']['ran'] == 3, report['executed']

"""Tests that would catch a raise, missed: for one change, the tests that fail when its changed lines raise, less the
tests AMU had as candidates on the head.

Usage: python raise_missed.py --head TREE --patch PATCH --report REPORT.json --python PY [--runner pytest|django-runtests]
       [--workers N]

Each hunk's first changed statement on the head gets ``raise RuntimeError('AMU-RAISE <path>:<line>')`` in front of it,
at its indentation; a statement that starts a definition gets it as the first line of its body instead, so it raises
when called. Statements at module or class level are not given one (a raise at import fails every test importing the
module, which says nothing about one line); they are counted under ``not_injected``. Then the whole suite runs once on
the head copy with every raise in place, and a test that fails with the marker in its failure text is a catcher. A raise
in one hunk can keep another from running in the same test, so the catchers are a lower bound per hunk; their union is
what is compared.

Prints JSON: catchers, candidates, missed (catchers not among the candidates), and per hunk where its raise went.
"""
import argparse
import ast
import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from pathlib import Path

MARK = 'AMU-RAISE'


def hunks(patch):
    """{path: [first added line of each hunk]} for production .py files, from a unified diff."""
    found, path, new_line, first = {}, None, 0, None
    for line in patch.splitlines():
        if line.startswith('+++ '):
            raw = line[4:].split('\t')[0]
            path = raw[2:] if raw.startswith('b/') else None if raw == '/dev/null' else raw
            if path and (not path.endswith('.py') or re.search(r'(^|/)(tests?|testing)/|(^|/)test_[^/]*\.py$|_test\.py$|conftest\.py$', path)):
                path = None
        elif line.startswith('@@') and path:
            new_line = int(re.match(r'@@ -\d+(?:,\d+)? \+(\d+)', line)[1])
            first = None
        elif path and line.startswith('+') and not line.startswith('+++'):
            if first is None:
                first = new_line
                found.setdefault(path, []).append(new_line)
            new_line += 1
        elif path and line.startswith(' '):
            new_line += 1
    return found


def inject(text, lines, path):
    """``text`` with a raise before the first statement starting on or after each of ``lines`` within its hunk."""
    tree = ast.parse(text)
    statements = []
    parents = {}
    for node in ast.walk(tree):
        for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node):
            parents[child] = node
        if isinstance(node, ast.stmt):
            statements.append(node)
    rows, where = text.splitlines(True), []
    inserts = {}
    for line in lines:
        hit = sorted((s for s in statements if s.lineno >= line), key=lambda s: (s.lineno, -s.col_offset))
        if not hit or hit[0].lineno > line + 30:
            where.append(dict(line=line, at=None, why='no statement'))
            continue
        node = hit[0]
        if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
            body = node.body[0]
            if isinstance(body, ast.Expr) and isinstance(getattr(body, 'value', None), ast.Constant) and len(node.body) > 1:
                body = node.body[1]
            node = body
        owner = parents.get(node)
        if isinstance(owner, (ast.Module, ast.ClassDef)):
            where.append(dict(line=line, at=None, why='module or class level'))
            continue
        indent = re.match(r'\s*', rows[node.lineno - 1])[0]
        inserts[node.lineno] = f"{indent}raise RuntimeError('{MARK} {path}:{line}')\n"
        where.append(dict(line=line, at=node.lineno))
    for at in sorted(inserts, reverse=True):
        rows.insert(at - 1, inserts[at])
    return ''.join(rows), where


def catchers_pytest(python, tree, workers, report):
    command = [python, '-m', 'pytest', '-q', '-p', 'no:cacheprovider', '-p', 'no:randomly', f'--junitxml={report}']
    if workers > 1:
        command += ['-n', str(workers)]
    subprocess.run(command, cwd=tree, capture_output=True, timeout=6 * 3600)
    found = set()
    for case in ET.parse(report).getroot().iter('testcase'):
        said = ''.join((c.get('message') or '') + (c.text or '') for c in case if c.tag in ('failure', 'error'))
        if MARK not in said:
            continue
        parts = case.get('classname', '').split('.')
        for cut in range(len(parts), 0, -1):
            if (tree/('/'.join(parts[:cut]) + '.py')).is_file():
                found.add('::'.join(['/'.join(parts[:cut]) + '.py', *parts[cut:], case.get('name', '').split('[')[0]]))
                break
    return found


def catchers_django(python, tree, workers):
    done = subprocess.run([python, 'runtests.py', '-v', '2', '--noinput', f'--parallel={workers}'], cwd=tree/'tests',
                          capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=6 * 3600)
    output = done.stdout + done.stderr
    found = set()
    for block in re.split(r'^={20,}$', output, flags=re.M)[1:]:
        match = re.search(r'^(?:ERROR|FAIL): (\w+) \(([\w.]+)\)', block, re.M)
        if not match or MARK not in block:
            continue
        label = match[2]
        parts = label.split('.')
        for cut in range(len(parts) - 1, 0, -1):
            if (tree/'tests'/('/'.join(parts[:cut]) + '.py')).is_file():
                found.add('::'.join(['tests/' + '/'.join(parts[:cut]) + '.py', *parts[cut:]]))
                break
    return found


def main(argv=None):
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    p.add_argument('--head', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--patch', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--report', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--python', required=True)
    p.add_argument('--runner', default='pytest')
    p.add_argument('--workers', type=int, default=1)
    args = p.parse_args(argv)
    patch = Path(args.patch).read_text()
    report = json.loads(Path(args.report).read_text())
    candidates = set(report.get('candidate_sources') or {}) or {row['id'] for row in report.get('tests') or []}
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix='amu-raise-') as scratch:
        tree = Path(scratch)/'tree'
        shutil.copytree(args.head, tree, symlinks=True, ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns('.git', '.amu', '__pycache__'))
        placed = {}
        for path, lines in hunks(patch).items():
            text = (tree/path).read_text()
            changed, where = inject(text, lines, path)
            (tree/path).write_text(changed)
            placed[path] = where
        injected = sum(1 for rows in placed.values() for row in rows if row.get('at'))
        if args.runner == 'django-runtests':
            caught = catchers_django(args.python, tree, args.workers)
        else:
            caught = catchers_pytest(args.python, tree, args.workers, Path(scratch)/'raise.xml')
    missed = sorted(caught - candidates)
    print(json.dumps(dict(injected=injected, not_injected=sum(1 for rows in placed.values() for row in rows if not row.get('at')),
                          catchers=len(caught), candidates=len(candidates), missed=len(missed), missed_tests=missed[:50],
                          placed=placed), indent=1))


if __name__ == '__main__':
    sys.exit(main())
